answer: Duplicate or recycled hashes are rejected, and any attempt to spin up clones triggers a "ripple" penalty that slashes the stake across linked identities. Each agent must stake a bond and submit a unique proof-of-work "sonnet" hash tied to its identity, which the network verifies against a shared "atlas" registry of prior submissions. Attacker costs thus scale linearly with each fake agent, making mass sybil creation economically unviable while honest agents recover their bond over time.
